chunks: And in the narration of Abū Khadījah Sālim ibn Mukram al-Jammāl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
Lying against Allah, His Messenger, and the awṣiyāʾ عليهم السلام is among the major sins.

key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the Exalted, against whom false attribution is a grave sin
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: the successors or designated trustees, referring to the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.الْكَبَائِرِ: the major sins, meaning grave offenses with serious spiritual consequence
key_terms.الْكَذِبُ: falsehood or lying; here, falsely attributing something to sacred authority
key_terms.رَسُولِهِ: His Messenger, meaning the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Is lying about Allah, the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the Imams عليهم السلام considered a major sin in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that fabricating lies against Allah, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and the awṣiyāʾ عليهم السلام is counted among the major sins. It underscores the grave moral and religious seriousness of falsely attributing statements, rulings, or teachings to divine and sacred authorities.
